transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because things have been pretty tense at home lately. It's about my wife. 

I know she says her late meetings and these little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but... for the past year, they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It really feels like there’s a private signal in them, meant to tell me something she just won’t say directly. She thinks I'm reading too much into it and wanted me to talk to someone, so I agreed to come in.
Have you noticed any other unusual experiences, such as hearing voices when no one else is around or feeling like your thoughts are being broadcast to others?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices, and I definitely don't feel like anyone can hear my thoughts. My mind is my own. 

It's really just... what I was saying before. It's about the patterns in her schedule and the specific words she uses. I'm not hearing things that aren't there, I'm just noticing what is actually happening right in front of me.
Do you feel like other people in your life, perhaps at work or in your neighborhood, are also acting in ways that suggest they are hiding things from you or working against you?

No, not at all. The people at work—the other teaching assistants and the professors—they're just doing their jobs. And the neighbors are fine. I don't think anyone is out to get me or... or hiding things from me in general. It's really just this one specific situation at home with my wife. I don't have any problems with anyone else.
Looking back over the past several years, before this situation with your wife began, have you generally felt that people in your life were likely to be manipulative, deceptive, or untrustworthy?

No, I haven't. I mean, before this started about a year ago, I never really thought about people like that. I've always had pretty normal relationships, you know? I trust my friends, I get along with the people I work with at the university. I've never been the type to think everyone is out to trick me or lie to me. That's why this whole thing with her is so... confusing. It's completely out of the ordinary for us.
Do you believe that your wife is being unfaithful to you with someone else?

No, no, I don't think she's having an affair. It's not about another man or... or anything romantic like that. It's just... the things I mentioned. The schedule changes, the way she talks to me, the feeling that she's hiding her real intentions. But I don't believe she's cheating on me.
Do you feel that these signals you are noticing in your wife's behavior are part of a larger plan or message involving other people or organizations?

No, I don't think it's anything like that. I don't think there's some... secret organization or anything involved. It's just her. It's just between the two of us. I really don't think anyone else has anything to do with what she's doing.
When these thoughts about your wife's hidden messages come into your mind, do you find them distressing or unwanted, and do you ever try to resist or push these thoughts away?

I don't really try to push them away, no. I mean, the situation itself is stressful, obviously, because I don't understand why she's doing it. But the thoughts aren't... I wouldn't call them unwanted in the sense that I'm trying to block them out. 

They're just things I'm noticing. It's just what's happening right in front of me. So I don't really try to resist thinking about it, I'm just... I'm just trying to figure out what she actually means.
